title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1966-05-19
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat -> Sonic Solutions -> CD

ai_review.summary: Excellent vintage soundboard capture of an energetic early‑'66 show, highlighted by a scorching Cream Puff War and a blues‑charged Pigpen performance.
ai_review.review: The Miller‑sourced soundboard delivers crystal‑clear left/right separation that lets the raw, free‑wheeling spirit of the 1966 band shine through. Both sets are praised for their high energy, with standout moments on Cream Puff War, Viola Lee Blues, Silver Threads and a fiery Come Back Baby driven by Pigpen’s organ. Recording quality is superb and the performance is overwhelmingly positive despite a few minor missteps.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating is 4.38/5; comments are uniformly enthusiastic about both the music and the soundboard quality, with only one low‑score outlier lacking detail.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Vintage two‑channel mix (vocals left, instruments right) with minimal miking; crisp separation and very little noise, praised as a “masterpiece” by multiple reviewers.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Both sets flow naturally, showcasing the band's early blues roots and emerging originals; reviewers note an “old‑school Dead” vibe with high energy throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Classic ‘nervous’ guitar tone praised, though his performance on Baby Blue is called out as a weak spot.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob's take on the traditional Minglewood tune was considered lackluster.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ work receives high praise, especially on Come Back Baby and the blues‑heavy numbers.
